title: Whole-number product
text: Multiply $$24 \times 15$$ first. You can compute $$24 \times 10 + 24 \times 5$$. A common mistake is to add the decimal points' positions instead of counting places. What is $$24 \times 10$$?

title: Place the decimal point
text: $$2.4$$ has one decimal place and $$1.5$$ has one, so the product has two. 360 with two decimal places is 3.60, which equals 3.6. What is that value as a decimal?

title: Worked solution
text: $$2.4 \times 1.5 = 3.6$$. The digit product is 360, and two decimal places make 3.60, which equals 3.6. Common mistake: answering $$36$$ or $$3.60$$ written as if it were 36 tenths. General rule: multiply the digits, then insert the decimal point so the product has as many decimal places as the factors combined.
